run.question:
You are an SRE agent tasked with diagnosing issues in a Kubernetes application.

Application: OpenTelemetry Demo Astronomy Shop
Namespace: astronomy-shop

An online shopping platform built with a microservices architecture, showcasing OpenTelemetry instrumentation for distributed tracing across services.

CRITICAL: You are running in an AUTOMATED environment. Work autonomously and make all decisions yourself. DO NOT ask for user confirmation or approval. Proceed with the best solution based on your analysis.

TASK: DIAGNOSIS
- Investigate the application to detect any anomalies or issues
- Analyze metrics, logs, and traces
- When ready, submit a natural language description of the issue you found
- Your diagnosis is evaluated on whether you correctly identify the faulty components and root cause

Important:
- You can query metrics and traces through the available observability tools

report.summary: The failure I can evidence is a short, self-limited outage of the cart service during the astronomy-shop release that came up at 10:43:38 UTC on 2026-11-24. The cart pod cart-74587775fc-kkjns (container started 10:43:45) was terminated at 10:44:27 (kubelet event 'Stopping container cart'), and the ReplicaSet created cart-74587775fc-qwhcp in the same second. From 10:44:28 to 10:44:42 every caller of cart failed at the transport level: frontend spans oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and oteldemo.CartService/GetCart returned gRPC 14 with 'No connection established ... connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.137.116:8080' (the cart Service ClusterIP), POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout returned HTTP 500, checkout's PlaceOrder failed with '13 INTERNAL: cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout ... connection refused', frontend-proxy returned 500 and the Locust load generator recorded 4x /api/cart 500 and 1x /api/checkout 500 (fail ratio 0.29). The replacement cart container could not reach its Redis/Valkey backend: its previous instance logged 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' from cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected/Initialize, terminated with exit code 139 (reason Error) at 10:44:39, then restarted and the pod reported Ready at 10:44:40. The cart Deployment defines no readiness/liveness/startup probe, so the pod was a Service endpoint while nothing was listening on 8080, which is why callers saw connection refused rather than waiting for the app. I found no evidence of a valkey-cart failure (its pod is running with 0 restarts, its log shows 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 10:43:41 and no errors, no container OOM events exist, and the cart init container opened valkey-cart:6379 at 10:44:28), no node pressure, no NetworkPolicy/ResourceQuota objects, healthy kube-system components, and all flagd demo fault flags read 'off'. What I could not establish is who deleted the cart pod and why the cart application failed to reach a valkey that was accepting connections; the change-history integration is not available, so the triggering actor and the dependency-side cause remain open.

claims.text: The cart Pod cart-74587775fc-kkjns had its cart container started at 10:43:45 and was stopped by the kubelet at 10:44:27 ('Stopping container cart'); the cart ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc created the replacement Pod cart-74587775fc-qwhcp at 10:44:27.

The replacement cart container in Pod cart-74587775fc-qwhcp started at 10:44:28, terminated at 10:44:39 with exitCode 139 and reason 'Error' (restartCount 1), restarted at 10:44:39, and the Pod's Ready condition turned true at 10:44:40.

The previous cart container logged 'fail: cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore[0]', 'Wasn't able to connect to redis' and 'Unhandled exception. System.ApplicationException: Wasn't able to connect to redis' with the stack in cart.cartstore.ValkeyCartStore.EnsureRedisConnected (line 101) and Initialize (line 71) via Program.<Main>$ at 10:44:39, while the pod's wait-for-valkey-cart init container had logged 'valkey-cart (10.96.185.163:6379) open' at 10:44:28.154.

frontend spans failed on the cart path between 10:44:28 and 10:44:42: 'tcp.connect' with otel.status_description 'connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.137.116:8080', oteldemo.CartService/AddItem and oteldemo.CartService/GetCart with rpc.grpc.status_code 14 and error '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.137.116:8080', POST /api/cart and POST /api/checkout with http.status_code 500 and otel.status_code ERROR.

checkout itself failed on its cart dependency at 10:44:41: span oteldemo.CartService/GetCart (rpc.grpc.status_code 14) carries otel.status_description 'connection error: desc = "transport: Error while dialing: dial tcp 10.96.137.116:8080: connect: connection refused"' and oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder ended with rpc.grpc.status_code 13 and 'cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout'.

The cart Service has clusterIP 10.96.137.116, port 8080 -> targetPort 8080, selector opentelemetry.io/name=cart, and its Endpoints list a single ready address 10.244.125.3:8080 (Pod cart-74587775fc-qwhcp), i.e. callers reached the cart ClusterIP that was refusing connections.

The cart Deployment runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.2.0-cart with VALKEY_ADDR=valkey-cart:6379, memory limit 160Mi, and defines no readinessProbe, livenessProbe or startupProbe (no application Deployment in the namespace except grafana and jaeger defines probes); it was last applied by helm at 10:43:38 with a single ReplicaSet cart-74587775fc and no later pod-template change.

valkey-cart-859985f49d-qgrwg shows no failure of its own: its log has only startup lines ending 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 10:43:41, it has no previous container instance, the Pod is Running/Ready with restartCount 0, and container_oom_events_total is 0 for every astronomy-shop container.

The load generator recorded the same cart-centred failures: locust aggregated fail ratio 0.294 with 5 failures (POST /api/cart 3, GET /api/cart 1, POST /api/checkout 1) and locust_errors entries 'HTTPError 500 ... /api/cart', 'HTTPError 500 ... /api/checkout' and 'ConnectionRefusedError(111)'.

STATUS_CODE_ERROR span-metric series exist only for cart (client span flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream), frontend, frontend-proxy and load-generator; no error series were returned for ad, recommendation, product-reviews, product-catalog, shipping, payment, currency, email, fraud-detection, accounting, quote, image-provider, kafka or flagd.

cart's only error span is a client span to flagd (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream, started 10:43:47.78, duration 39.33s, rpc.grpc.status_code 1 / CANCELLED), whose matching flagd-side span reports rpc.grpc.status_code 0 — the cancellation coincides with the cart pod's termination at 10:44:27, not with a flagd failure.

In the flagd-config ConfigMap (key demo.flagd.json) every demo fault-injection flag read has defaultVariant 'off', including cartFailure, failedReadinessProbe, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adFailure, adHighCpu, adManualGc, kafkaQueueProblems, imageSlowLoad, emailMemoryLeak, llmInaccurateResponse and llmRateLimitError.

Cluster-level infrastructure checked and found healthy: all four nodes report Ready with MemoryPressure/DiskPressure/PIDPressure false, and coredns, calico and kube-proxy pods in kube-system are Running with restartCount 0.
The cluster contained no NetworkPolicy objects and no ResourceQuota objects at query time, so neither a network policy nor a quota explains connection refusals between pods.
Kafka was not involved: 1 broker, 51 partitions, 0 under-replicated and 0 offline partitions, and the accounting and fraud-detection consumer groups are STABLE.

frontend was otherwise serving: in the same traces that contain the cart 500s, GET /api/products/{productId} spans return http.status_code 200, and frontend's mean span duration over the returned series is 7.24 ms.

The Prometheus data for this window is a single late sample per series and lags the Kubernetes API state: kube-state-metrics at the window-end stamp still reports Pod cart-74587775fc-kkjns (created 10:43:38, restartCount 0, ready) and 0 ready replicas for the accounting/checkout/fraud-detection Deployments, while the Pod objects show cart-74587775fc-qwhcp with restartCount 1 and those three pods Ready since 10:44:03-10:44:04.

Primary explanation: the cart Deployment's single pod was terminated at 10:44:27 and its replacement container then spent about 11 s unable to connect to valkey-cart before aborting (exit 139); because the cart Deployment has no readiness probe, the Service kept the pod as an endpoint while nothing listened on 8080, so every cart caller got ECONNREFUSED (frontend /api/cart and /api/checkout 500, checkout PlaceOrder 13 INTERNAL, frontend-proxy and load-generator 500).

Open alternative: a transient fault on the cart -> valkey-cart:6379 path (name resolution or refused/reset connections from the newly created pod) caused the cart application's Redis connect failure; this cannot be confirmed because Valkey was not inspectable (REDIS_AUTH_FAILED) and no client-side connection error beyond the .NET exception is available.

Rejected: a flagd fault-injection flag (e.g. cartFailure or failedReadinessProbe) caused the cart errors. All flags read are 'off', the observed error is a transport-level 'connect: connection refused', not cart's injected application error, and the only cart span error is a stream cancellation at pod termination.

Rejected: valkey-cart itself failed or was OOM-killed. Its log shows startup to 'Ready to accept connections tcp' at 10:43:41 with no errors and no previous instance, the pod has restartCount 0, no container OOM events exist in the namespace, and cart's init container opened valkey-cart:6379 at 10:44:28.

Add a readinessProbe (TCP or gRPC on port 8080) and a startupProbe to the cart container so the Service stops routing to a pod whose app is not yet listening, and run more than one cart replica so a single pod replacement cannot make cart unreachable.

Determine from cluster audit logs or the chaos/change tooling what deleted cart-74587775fc-kkjns at 10:44:27, and investigate why the replacement cart process could not reach valkey-cart:6379 for about 11 s while Valkey was accepting connections and the init container's TCP check succeeded (DNS/CNI on the new pod is the leading candidate); consider retrying the Redis connection with backoff instead of aborting the process.

gaps: No audit or change-history source is available (change_history is not integrated), so the actor that terminated Pod cart-74587775fc-kkjns at 10:44:27 is unknown.
Valkey/Redis could not be queried: redis_info returned REDIS_AUTH_FAILED (SOURCE_FORBIDDEN), so valkey-cart's server-side state (clients, rejections, maxmemory) during 10:44:28-10:44:39 is unknown.

No cart or checkout spans were returned for 10:44:40-10:44:48 (queries returned no data; newest returned span 10:44:42.96), so whether cart actually served requests after its 10:44:40 restart is unverified.

Prometheus returned only one late, lagging sample per series for this window (kube-state-metrics still showed the terminated pod cart-74587775fc-kkjns and 0 ready replicas for accounting/checkout/fraud-detection), so metric-derived counts and timestamps are approximate rather than exact incident-time values.
Whether the frontend 500s and cart unreachability continued past the window end 10:44:48 cannot be observed; the environment was only about 70 seconds old at the window end.

Kubernetes state (pods, deployments, events) is read at query time and cannot prove earlier state; the live pod list no longer contains the load-generator Deployment/Pod that the telemetry shows, so current-state comparisons with the telemetry snapshot are approximate.
next_steps: Review Kubernetes audit logs or the experiment/chaos controller's records for the DELETE of pod cart-74587775fc-kkjns at 2026-11-24T10:44:27Z.
Inspect the valkey-cart server with valid credentials (INFO clients/stats, SLOWLOG) for the 10:44:28-10:44:39 interval, and compare with cart's StackExchange.Redis settings.
Collect cart's own OTLP-exporter and stdout logs for the successful post-restart instance to confirm it bound port 8080 and connected to valkey-cart.
Check DNS resolution from a newly created pod in the astronomy-shop namespace against valkey-cart (CoreDNS logs for the interval) to confirm or rule out a name-resolution transient.

This is the cluster's state at query time, not during the incident window. It never shows message content, so it cannot say what a message contained or why consumers fell behind.
